title: AtlasULP: Domain-aware Universal Link Prediction via Relation Atlas
abstract: arXiv:2611.07347v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Link prediction (LP) is a widely applied task in graph learning. Conventional LP approaches typically follow a dataset-specific paradigm, requiring independent training for each graph and incurring high computational and maintenance costs in large-scale applications. Motivated by these limitations, recent work explores Universal Link Prediction (ULP), aiming to enable training-free inference on arbitrary unseen graphs. However, existing methods primarily rely on subgraph sampling strategies to construct universal representations, which are unable to capture higher-order information due to the exponential growth of higher-order neighborhoods. As a result, they often under-perform on graphs where long-range signals are essential, such as biological networks. Moreover, their prediction models are typically domain-agnostic and lack the ability to adapt to different graph domains, leading to limited generalization. To address these challenges

translated_title: AtlasULP：基于关系图谱的领域感知通用链接预测
translated_abstract: 链接预测（LP）是图学习中一项被广泛应用的任务。传统链接预测方法通常遵循特定于数据集的范式，需要对每个图进行独立训练，在大规模应用中导致高昂的计算和维护成本。受这些局限性的启发，近期工作探索了通用链接预测（ULP），旨在实现对任意未见过的图进行无需训练的推理。然而，现有方法主要依赖子图采样策略来构建通用表示，由于高阶邻域的指数级增长，这些方法无法捕获高阶信息。因此，它们在远程信号至关重要的图上往往表现不佳，例如生物网络。此外，其预测模型通常是领域无关的，缺乏适应不同图领域的能力，导致泛化能力有限。为了解决这些挑战……
tldr: 该论文提出AtlasULP，通过关系图谱捕获高阶信息并实现领域感知能力，使模型能够在无需训练的情况下对任意未见图进行推理，克服了现有通用链接预测方法无法捕捉长距离依赖和泛化受限的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes AtlasULP, a domain-aware universal link prediction method that captures higher-order information via relation atlases, enabling training-free inference on arbitrary unseen graphs and overcoming the limitations of existing approaches in capturing long-range signals and generalizing across domains.
